note: The Scale Room stops, smallest to largest. Facts stated plainly; sizes are diameters or characteristic lengths.

stops.fact: A whole beach is a crowd of these, each one a mountain worn down to almost nothing.
stops.name: A grain of sand

stops.fact: She visits fifty to a hundred flowers on a single trip, and remembers the way home by the sun.
stops.name: A honeybee

stops.fact: The distance from your wrist to your middle fingertip is close to one ten-thousandth of the distance you will walk in a lifetime.
stops.name: Your hand

stops.fact: Small enough to hold in two hands; already contains everything needed to become someone you cannot yet imagine.
stops.name: A newborn child

stops.fact: Nearly every threshold you have ever crossed was made to roughly the measure of a person, plus a little hope.
stops.name: A door

stops.fact: Its heart weighs about eleven kilograms, built to lift blood all the way up to a dreaming head.
stops.name: A giraffe

stops.fact: From the street it looks still. Inside, it is mostly weather: warmth, argument, soup, sleep.
stops.name: A house

stops.fact: The largest animal known to have ever lived on Earth. Its tongue weighs about as much as an elephant.
stops.name: A blue whale

stops.fact: It grows about fifteen centimetres taller in summer, as the iron warms and stretches toward the sun.
stops.name: The Eiffel Tower

stops.fact: The mountain is still rising, about four millimetres a year, as two continents lean on each other.
stops.name: Mount Everest

stops.fact: It is drifting away from us about as fast as your fingernails grow. The tides are its long goodbye, still holding hands.
stops.name: The Moon

stops.fact: Eleven Earths would fit across its face. Its great storm has been blowing for at least three hundred years.
stops.name: Jupiter

stops.fact: A million Earths would fit inside it. The light warming your face left its surface eight minutes ago.
stops.name: The Sun

stops.fact: Not a time but a distance: how far light travels in a year of running without rest.
stops.name: One light-year

stops.fact: Our whole galaxy, turning slowly. Every star you have ever seen at night is a near neighbour.
stops.name: The Milky Way

stops.fact: Everything we can, even in principle, ever see. Beyond this edge there is more; it is simply not ours to know. Yet.
stops.name: The observable universe
